item.title: red warning - severe thunderstorm - in effect
item.description:
At 7:26 p.m. MDT, an extremely dangerous thunderstorm is located near Barnwell. This extremely dangerous thunderstorm is moving east at 45 km/h. Damaging wind gusts, baseball size or greater hail and heavy rain are possible.
Locations and nearby areas that could be impacted include: Barnwell, Wrentham, Skiff
###
Driving conditions will be difficult. Buildings and/or many trees will be destroyed. Large hail will cause significant damage and injury.
Severe thunderstorm warnings are issued when imminent or occurring thunderstorms are expected to produce damaging hail, wind or rain.
Severe thunderstorms can produce tornadoes.
Area: (Co. of Lethbridge near Coaldale, M.D. of Taber near Taber and Barnwell, M.D. of Taber near Grassy Lake and Hwys 877 and 513, Co. of Warner near Wrentham, Co. of Forty Mile near Skiff, new active threat area, continued active threat area)

item.title: Kings County Memorial Hospital parking lot pavement work underway
item.description:
Kings County Memorial Hospital parking lot pavement work underway ddgillis Wed, 08/12/2026 - 15:40

Pavement work is now underway in the Kings County Memorial Hospital (KCMH) parking lot and is expected to be completed within approximately one week, weather permitting.

During this time, sections of the patient parking area will be temporarily closed, resulting in a reduced number of available parking spaces. These areas will remain inaccessible until the paving work has been completed.

To ensure the safety of patients, visitors, staff, and contractors, traffic control personnel and signage will be in place throughout the project to help direct vehicles and pedestrians.

Patients and visitors are encouraged to plan ahead, allow extra time for parking, and follow all posted signage and directions from traffic control personnel.

Health PEI appreciates the public's patience and cooperation as this work is completed to improve the hospital parking area.

item.title: Tourism PEI introduces new bench installations inspired by Carley Fortune's bestselling novel
item.description:
Tourism PEI introduces new bench installations inspired by Carley Fortune's bestselling novel ddgillis Wed, 08/12/2026 - 14:50

Tourism PEI is inviting visitors to step inside the pages of one of the world’s most popular summer reads. Tourism PEI, in collaboration with bestselling Canadian author Carley Fortune, unveiled a series of handcrafted benches at locations featured in This Summer Will Be Different, creating a new literary tourism experience that celebrates the Island's landscapes, communities and growing profile as a destination for readers from around the globe.

The first bench installations can now be found at Basin Head Provincial Park and Point Prim Lighthouse, two iconic settings where visitors can pause and experience some of the landscapes that helped bring This Summer Will Be Different to life. More than places to sit, the installations serve as story markers, encouraging visitors to linger a little longer, soak in the view and experience the Island through the eyes of the novel's beloved characters.

Additional benches will be unveiled in the coming months at other locations featured in This Summer Will Be Different, creating a growing literary trail across western Prince Edward Island, further strengthening the connection between the story and the places that inspired it. Islanders and travelers alike are invited to discover what's next, explore new corners of the Island, and experience what makes PEI so special.

For more information about the PEI locations featured in This Summer Will Be Different, and trip ideas, visit TourismPEI.com

Quotes:


"We're delighted to welcome Carley Fortune back to Prince Edward Island as we unveil these beautiful locally crafted benches. Her novel has sparked tremendous interest in the places and experiences that make our Island special, and these installations give both residents and visitors a chance to connect with the story while exploring some of PEI's most iconic destinations. We look forward to expanding this literary trail with additional locations in western Prince Edward Island in the months ahead."

-Minister of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism Ernie Hudson

“I'm so honoured This Summer Will Be Different is now part of the Prince Edward Island landscape thanks to these stunning benches. The Island has been an inspiration to me since I first visited, and I hope these benches give others a place to pause and reflect on their own journey to this magical place.” 

-Carley Fortune, Author, This Summer Will Be Different

"I’ve been building my Island love story since the moment I landed. The natural beauty inspires my work, and I’m surrounded by an incredible community that has encouraged me to make this dream my career."

-Mel Burke, Black Cat Woodcraft

 

Media Contacts:

Department of Fisheries, Rural Development and Tourism 
Government of Prince Edward Island
Jedwards@gov.pe.ca

Stephen Fertelmes

sfertelmes@jillfritzopr.com  

Backgrounder

Carley Fortune biography

Carley Fortune is the #1 New York Times bestselling author of Every Summer After, One Golden Summer, This Summer Will Be Different and Meet Me at the Lake. Her books have sold more than five million copies, have been translated into 35 languages across more than 100 territories, and adapted for television. Her fifth novel, Our Perfect Storm, was released May 10 and was an instant #1 New York Times bestseller. The first season of Every Year After, the series based on her novel Every Summer After, hit #1 on Prime Video worldwide and was renewed for a second season. This Summer Will Be Different is currently in production and will stream on Netflix as a ten-episode series. Fortune is an Executive Producer on both projects.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
